newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says killed 68 rebel Kurds in two days.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says killed 68 rebel Kurds in two days.

text.p: Turkey's security forces killed 68 Kurdish guerrillas in fighting over the weekend in the southeast of the country, the emergency rule governor's office said on Monday.
The statements said troops, backed by air power, killed 33 members of the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) in the province of Van, near Turkey's border with Iran.
In separate clashes, security forces killed a further 26 guerrillas in the southeastern province of Hakkari and a further three in Sirnak province, it said.
There was no mention of military casualties.
Officials at the governor's office in Diyarbakir earlier said six guerrillas had been killed late on Sunday in the southeastern province of Bingol, two of them women.
The clashes on Turkish soil take place as Turkish forces are engaged in a six-week operation against the PKK in neighbouring northern Iraq, which the rebels use as a base for raids into Turkey.

State-run Anatolian news agency on Monday reported the funerals of two soldiers killed in fighting with the PKK. One of the men was killed in Diyarbakir province, but no details of when the deaths took place or where the other died were given.
More than 24,000 people have been killed in the conflict between Turkish security forces and the PKK, fighting for 12 years for autonomy or independence in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
